brief: UBS's Friday hedge fund flow note: hedge funds continued cutting AI beta, led by Semis (-0.8std), Memory (-1.0std) and Hardware (-1.2std), but the mix shifted from over 90% long selling to roughly 50/50 long selling and shorting. Hyperscalers were small net bought (+0.3std) as funds rotated into higher-quality names with available compute and stronger build profiles, extending a trend seen since early October. Power names were net bought (+1.7std), about 70% of it from long buying. Hedge funds bottom-fished selectively and added relative-value trades across the AI value chain. Overall gross exposure to US equities rose +1.9std, the 6th-largest re-risking day YTD, split +2std short exposure and +1std long exposure, so the add was market-neutral/RV rather than directional; Friday's increase in short exposure was the largest since June 15, before the summer unwind. UBS's Zain Nizami flagged rising correlations as a risk that crowded Semis-vs-Software and Semis-vs-Hyperscalers trades spill into broader portfolio de-risking, and recommended buying Semis against selling the recent hedging beneficiaries, noting Semis net exposure is back near July and Liberation Day lows while Hyperscaler and Software exposure stays high.
